messages:
Maya Chen: Heads-up — getting multiple customer p99 latency reports for requests hitting sa-east-1 egress since ~09:30 UTC. Raised by CS, includes TLS handshake time spikes (~200-400ms increase). Opening thread for triage.

Lucas Moreno: Customer: "we're seeing sudden slow connects from Santiago -> sa-east. Every request has an extra ~300ms before first byte." I asked for a curl tracer; they sent this: 

```
curl -w '\\nlookup:%{time_namelookup} conn:%{time_connect} appconn:%{time_appconnect} ttfb:%{time_starttransfer}\n' -s -o /dev/null https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
# result: lookup:0.012 conn:0.050 appconn:0.380 ttfb:0.420
```

Lucas Moreno: They also ran `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.example:443 -msg -showcerts` and measured the handshake time ~370ms.

Tiff Carter: Thanks. Can someone run quick egress path traceroutes from sa-east nodes and a few customer vantage points? I suspect cross-ISP handoffs or a regional anycast shift. @Riley you on network? :eyes: 

Riley Nguyen: On it. Kicking off traceroute from edge-01-sa-east and from a test VM in GCP-sa-east1. Also pulling edge envoy TLS timings for the last 15m.

Riley Nguyen: Traceroute (edge-01-sa-east -> customer IP):
```
1 10.0.0.1
2 100.64.0.5
3 185.72.12.1 (peer-isp)
4 198.51.100.8  120 ms  118 ms  119 ms
5 203.0.113.5   320 ms  318 ms  315 ms
```

Riley Nguyen: There's a clear hop with ~300ms. I'm seeing BGP flaps with a specific upstream peer (ASN 64501) around the same window. NetOps-Bot flagged consecutive route changes.

NetOps-Bot: Alert: BGP UPDATE count increased on peer ASN 64501 at 09:28 UTC. Flap count: 12 in 4m. 

Priya Kapoor: Any DNS anomalies? Could be a split-horizon or geo-DNS fallback to a further POP.

Maya Chen: Good call. Checking DNS resolution logs for api.redwood.example in sa-east region.

Maya Chen: DNS query latencies are fine (10-30ms), but large fraction of queries are resolving to egress IPs in us-east-1/sa-west pool unexpectedly, likely due to geoip mismatch or upstream resolver policy. That would cause longer routing.

Riley Nguyen: Correlating: BGP instability + some anycast / geo-DNS fallbacks = handshake path going cross-continent causing TLS RTT jump.

Lucas Moreno: Customer reports intermittent; some requests are fine, others slow. Matches routing flaps. They're pushing a live demo — want priority.

Tiff Carter: Mitigation plan: 1) Temporarily fail traffic for sa-east to dedicated regional pool (non-anycast VIP) to avoid upstream peer 64501. 2) Notify CS and affected customers. 3) NetOps engage ISP for flapping peer. 4) Longer-term: adjust geo-DNS health thresholds. Who can do (1) now?

Riley Nguyen: I can flip traffic to regional pool via control plane. Will do a canary first (5% -> 20% -> 100%). ETA 3m.

Deploy-Bot: Deploy queued: route-shift-sa-east -> canary(5%) by Riley Nguyen.

Riley Nguyen: Canary started. Observing handshake times (canary) dropping to ~40-60ms. p99 for canary routes now ~80ms. Non-canary still high.

Maya Chen: Nice. Please increase to 50% if stable. Also open a quick firewall rule check — ensure no extra NAT hairpin.

Riley Nguyen: Rolling to 50% now.

Priya Kapoor: I'm checking edge config: no NAT hairpin found. TLS termination still on our edge. No config drift.

Riley Nguyen: At 50% steady for 4m. Handshake times for shifted traffic stable. Increasing to 100% now.

Deploy-Bot: route-shift-sa-east -> 100% complete.

Tiff Carter: Great. Lucas, please let the customer know we pushed traffic to regional pool and should see improvements now — ask them to validate. :thumbsup:

Lucas Moreno: Noted. Sent update to customer; they replied "latency back to normal, thanks". cc @Maya.

Maya Chen: Marking mitigation as successful. Next steps: NetOps to follow up with ISP ASN 64501 on BGP flaps; infra to add a metric alert for geo-dns fallback rates (trigger if >5% of queries for region resolve outside region). Priya please file a runbook update for future automated regional failover.

NetOps-Bot: Ticket created: NETOPS-4621 to engage ASN 64501.

Priya Kapoor: Will create runbook draft and the geo-dns monitor query. Proposed monitor: fraction_of_queries_out_of_region / total_queries > 0.05 for 5m.

Tiff Carter: Also add a temporary dashboard widget for handshake latency broken down by route (anycast vs regional-pool). Helps catch regressions quicker.

Riley Nguyen: Logged: ENGNET-1489 for dashboard. I'm attaching traceroute output and BGP update logs to the ticket.

Maya Chen: Nice work team. Action owners recap: Riley = net failover + traceroutes + ENGNET-1489, Priya = runbook + geo-dns monitor, NetOps = NETOPS-4621 engage ISP, Lucas = customer comms. I'll close the alert after 30m of stable p99.

Support-Bot: Incident note appended to thread. Summary: regional egress latency caused by upstream BGP flaps affecting ASN 64501 -> temporary regional pool failover performed -> customer impact mitigated.

Maya Chen: Keeping this thread open until tickets close. If anyone observes reappearance ping here. Thanks all. :heart:
